optimized_brief: Have Team Durham audit the Allura plugin catalog READMEs and their infographics, then improve clarity, navigation, and consistent Allura branding. Use the approved brand identity and current repository evidence. Give each README a clear purpose, audience, install/use path and limits; make every visual explain one verified relationship with readable labels and alt text. Edit generated packages only through their owning source and exporter. Keep capability and runtime claims evidence-based. Have Munari independently review the result; return changed artifacts, checks, and remaining gaps.

excluded: New positioning, naming or logo design
Runtime installation or account GPT updates
New runtime, agent, provider or permission behavior

visual_review.method: Actual image files opened through the image-view tool; text claims compared with the approved brand gate and relevant README context.
visual_review.recommendation: Final documentation preserves all historical raster assets, links the unmodified official wordmark, and uses native Markdown tables and ordinary text instead of inline raster panels or Mermaid.
visual_review.readability_observation: At declared 900px width, headings remain readable but detailed labels and footers become small. Six consecutive panels occupy approximately 3400 vertical pixels before surrounding text.

official_mark.comparison: Byte-identical to the official allura-wordmark.png supplied by the approved brand skill
official_mark.finding: The exact official asset was preserved. Actual dark-theme review found insufficient inline legibility and excessive transparent padding; the final header uses a readable plain text title and links the original asset.

IMAGE X OF 6 placeholder, IMPLEMENTED badge, repetitive loop/sequence and small explanation strip.
Rules-to-every-action and immutable-lineage claims overstate what a plugin installation establishes.

Generic runtime illustration does not show the brief, discovery, strategy and production stages claimed in its alt text.
Arrow goes directly from Run to Release, bypassing Evidence/Review; gradients and implementation markers are also present.
Canonical-memory approval is presented as the brand workflow; flattened labels and badges cannot be maintained independently.
Presents version lineage as implemented without distinguishing the required contract from currently available update behavior.
Approved-memory labels, attached decisions and implementation markers imply evidence exists for every answer.
Eight narrow stages and raster labels crowd README width; the platform pipeline needs qualification separate from the installed skill.
Repeats adjacent controls without clarifying that the skill package supplies no scanner or server.
Small credential details and unlabeled fictional tenant/workspace examples make server controls appear to be package guarantees.
Useful verified-versus-unverified distinction, but all-evidence-verified language requires qualification and a precise source.
Dense branching, tiny footer, absolute never claim and redundant inventory boxes.
Observe-everything, immutable-proof and trusted-identities-across-every-layer wording gives unsupported universal assurances.
Unapproved gold, shadows, no official mark and unsupported trust-by-default, rollback and audit-ready claims.
Fake approval interface states HUMAN REVIEW / Approved by brooks-agent and depicts illustrative receipts, model selection and success states without execution evidence.
Obsolete Neo4j semantic-graph label, unapproved gold and small raster explanation strips.
